evals.prompt: I need to build a business case for our CFO to justify automating invoice processing. We have 3 staff in procurement spending 60% of their time manually processing invoices — about 500 per month, each taking roughly 15 minutes. Our fully loaded staff cost is £35k per person per year. I'm looking at an automation tool that costs £80k to implement and £12k per year to run. Can you help me build the business case?
evals.expected_output: A structured business case document with quantified problem statement, financial model showing costs and benefits, payback period calculation, risk mitigation, and executive summary
expectations: The output quantifies the current cost of manual invoice processing in annual monetary terms (e.g. FTE cost calculation)
The output calculates a break-even or payback period based on implementation cost vs annual savings
The output includes both implementation costs and annual run costs in a financial model
The output addresses at least one risk or stakeholder concern with a specific mitigation strategy
The output includes an executive summary or equivalent one-page overview section

evals.prompt: We're a mid-sized retailer and I'm trying to convince our board to invest in AI for our customer service operation. We handle 10,000 support tickets per month with 8 full-time agents at £28k each. I've been quoted £120k to implement an AI tool that claims to handle 40% of tickets automatically, with £15k per year ongoing support costs. Help me put together a convincing business case that addresses board-level concerns.
evals.expected_output: A persuasive business case targeting board-level decision-makers, with annual savings from ticket automation, ROI analysis, payback timeline, risk framing, and identification of board member concerns
expectations: The output calculates the annual cost saving from automating 40% of tickets (based on 8 FTE at £28k)
The output provides a payback period or break-even timeline
The output identifies board-level stakeholders and addresses their likely concerns or objections
The output uses conservative language or flags assumptions (e.g. acknowledges the 40% automation claim may not be achieved)
The output includes a section on implementation risk and how it is mitigated

evals.prompt: Help me build a business case to replace our Excel-based management reporting with Power BI. Currently each management report takes 2 full days to produce, we produce 20 reports per month, and the analyst doing this work earns £45k per year. Power BI Enterprise costs £50k per year as a SaaS subscription. Our CFO is skeptical and wants to see hard numbers and a clear ROI before he'll approve anything.
evals.expected_output: A rigorous, numbers-driven business case directed at a skeptical CFO, quantifying reporting time costs, net annual benefit after tool cost, payback period, and addressing typical CFO objections about ROI and risk
expectations: The output calculates the current annual cost of Excel-based reporting in FTE terms (days per month x analyst salary)
The output calculates net annual benefit (savings minus £50k Power BI cost)
The output provides a specific payback period figure
The output directly addresses the CFO's skepticism — naming ROI, hard numbers, or risk concerns
The output suggests a phased approach, pilot, or quick win to reduce perceived risk
